nodes.name: thm: main
nodes.statement:
Suppose $\mathbf{S} \subseteq \mathbf{V}$ is a single c-component. 
        $Q[\mathbf{S}]$ is g-identifiable from $(\mathbb{A}, \mathcal{G})$ if and only if there exists $\mathbf{A} \in \mathbb{A}$ such that $\mathbf{S} \subseteq \mathbf{A}$ and $Q[\mathbf{S}]$ is identifiable from $\mathcal{G}[\mathbf{A}]$.

nodes.name: lemma: prp3 - 1
nodes.statement:
Consider a causal graph $\mathcal{G}$ with observed variables $\mathbf{V}$.
            Suppose $\mathbf{X} \subseteq \mathbf{V}$ and $e:=(X_1,Z)$ is a directed edge such that $X_1\in\mathbf{X}$.
            
            $Q[\mathbf{X}]$ is g-identifiable from $(\mathbb{A},\mathcal{G})$ if and only if $Q[\mathbf{X}]$ is g-identifiable from $(\mathbb{A}, \mathcal{H})$, where $\mathcal{H}$ is the graph obtained by deleting $e$ from $\mathcal{G}$.

nodes.name: prp: 4
nodes.statement:
Suppose $\mathbf{S}_1,\cdots,\mathbf{S}_l$ are the c-components of $\mathbf{S} \subseteq \mathbf{V}$. 
        $Q[\mathbf{S}]$ is g-identifiable from $(\mathbb{A}, \mathcal{G})$ if and only if $Q[\mathbf{S}_i]$ is g-identifiable from $(\mathbb{A}, \mathcal{G})$ for all $i\in [1:l]$.

nodes.name: lemma: prp3 - 3
nodes.statement:
Assume $\mathbf{Y} \subset \mathbf{W} \subset \mathbf{V}$ such that for each $W \in \mathbf{W} \setminus \mathbf{Y}$, there exists a directed path in $\mathcal{G}[\mathbf{W}]$ from $W$ to a variable in $\mathbf{Y}$. 
            Then, the causal effect of $\mathbf{V} \setminus \mathbf{W}$ on $\mathbf{Y}$ is g-identifiable from $(\mathbb{A}, \mathcal{G})$ if and only if $Q[\mathbf{W}]$ is g-identifiable from $(\mathbb{A}, \mathcal{G})$.

nodes.name: lemma: prp3 - 2
nodes.statement: Suppose that $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ are disjoint subsets of $\mathbf{V}$. Let $(Y_1,Y_2)$ (i.e., $Y_1\rightarrow Y_2$) denotes a directed edge in $\mathcal{G}$, where $Y_1,Y_2 \in \mathbf{Y}$. Let $\mathcal{G}'$ denotes the resulting graph after removing edge $(Y_1,Y_2)$ from $\mathcal{G}$. If the causal effect of $\mathbf{X}$ on $\mathbf{Y}$ is not g-identifiable from $(\mathbb{A}, \mathcal{G}')$, then the causal effect of $\mathbf{X}$ on $\mathbf{Y} \setminus \{Y_1\}$ is not g-identifiable from $(\mathbb{A}, \mathcal{G})$.

nodes.name: prp: 3
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{Y}$ be two disjoint subsets of $\mathbf{V}$.
        The causal effect of $\mathbf{X}$ on $\mathbf{Y}$ is g-identifiable from $(\mathbb{A},\mathcal{G})$ if and only if $Q[\textit{Anc}_{\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{V} \setminus \mathbf{X}}}(\mathbf{Y})]$ is g-identifiable from $(\mathbb{A},\mathcal{G})$.

nodes.name: lem: simplify
nodes.statement: If $Q[\mathbf{S}]$ is not g-identifiable from $(\mathbb{A}', \mathcal{G}')$, then $Q[\mathbf{S}]$ is not g-identifiable from $(\mathbb{A}, \mathcal{G})$.

nodes.name: lemma: valid model
nodes.statement: The SEM constructed above belongs to $\mathbb{M}^+(\mathcal{G}')$.
